name: Rain Daniels
life: “I still remember an embroidered name too small for its owner to see.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Rain by a small Thursday habit. Rain checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I embroider names inside slippers. I'm going to ask first who can bend far enough to read them.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Rain has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Rain gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Rain is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To put labels where their wearers can see them.
family: Benjamin Lewis is Rain’s younger relative by marriage. Rain asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Benjamin remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The button card*, Benjamin says, “I collect glass buttons but gave away the best one because the boy needed a moon for his costume.”
connections: Cecil Hooper. The courier's route makes a practical place for easy-to-find names on labels.

reactions.situation: A patient opens the bag and finds two left slippers
reactions.response: Rain sets out the pair and asks the discharge worker to check the right foot too.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Rain stays with the rider after the people who saw the fall start drifting away.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Rain thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
